title: Minerals and Energy Resources
subject: geography
syllabus_note: Follows the CBSE 2025-26 Social Science (087) syllabus: this chapter is fully in the board examination (Geography: 17 marks + 3 map marks). Map work from this chapter: iron ore mines, coal mines, oil fields, and thermal and nuclear power plants (given here as text questions).

blocks.title: How many minerals did you use before breakfast?
blocks.body:
Your toothpaste has calcium carbonate and fluoride. The steel spoon came from iron ore, the aluminium pan from bauxite, the wires in your house from copper, and the electricity from coal, water or the sun.

Minerals are an indispensable part of our lives. But they take millions of years to form and we are using them up fast. This chapter explains how minerals occur, where India's main minerals are found, and how we get and save energy.

blocks.title: The father of India's nuclear programme
blocks.body:
Physicist **Homi Jehangir Bhabha** saw that India had little uranium but large reserves of **thorium** in the monazite sands of Kerala. He planned a long-term programme to use thorium for nuclear power.

He set up the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and the Atomic Energy Establishment at Trombay (later renamed the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre). India's nuclear power stations, like **Tarapur**, grew from his vision.
blocks.future: This chapter leads to careers in geology, mining engineering, petroleum engineering, nuclear science and renewable energy.

blocks.question: Why must we conserve minerals even though India has large reserves of some of them?
options: They are finite and non-renewable, and take millions of years to form
They are found only in India
blocks.explanation: The rate of replenishment is infinitely small compared with our rate of consumption.

sections.title: What minerals are and how they occur

blocks.title: Minerals and their modes of occurrence
blocks.body:
Geologists define a **mineral** as a **'homogenous, naturally occurring substance with a definable internal structure'**. Minerals are found in varied forms in nature, ranging from the **hardest diamond to the softest talc**. Rocks are combinations of homogenous substances called minerals.

Minerals are usually found in **'ores'**: an accumulation of any mineral mixed with other elements. The mineral content of the ore must be in sufficient concentration to make its extraction commercially viable.

**Modes of occurrence:**
1. **In igneous and metamorphic rocks:** minerals occur in the **cracks, crevices, faults or joints**. Smaller occurrences are called **veins** and larger ones **lodes**. They form when minerals in liquid, molten or gaseous form are forced upward through cavities towards the surface, then cool and solidify. Major metallic minerals like **tin, copper, zinc and lead** are obtained from veins and lodes.
2. **In sedimentary rocks:** minerals occur in **beds or layers**, formed by deposition, accumulation and concentration in horizontal strata. **Coal** and some forms of **iron ore** are concentrated after long periods under great heat and pressure. **Gypsum, potash salt and sodium salt** form as a result of **evaporation**, especially in arid regions.
3. **By decomposition of surface rocks:** soluble constituents are removed, leaving a residual mass of weathered material containing ores. **Bauxite** is formed this way.
4. **As alluvial deposits:** in the sands of valley floors and the base of hills; these are called **'placer deposits'** and generally contain minerals not corroded by water: **gold, silver, tin and platinum**.
5. **In ocean waters:** most minerals in ocean water are too widely diffused to be of economic significance, but **common salt, magnesium and bromine** are largely derived from ocean waters. The ocean beds are rich in **manganese nodules**.

**Rat-hole mining:** in parts of the north-east, like **Meghalaya** (Jowai and Cherrapunji), minerals are owned by individuals or communities. Coal is mined by family members in a **long, narrow tunnel** known as **'rat-hole' mining**.

blocks.question: Gold, silver, tin and platinum found in the sands of valley floors are called:
blocks.explanation: Placer deposits contain minerals not corroded by water.
option_feedback: These occur in cracks of igneous and metamorphic rocks.
These lie on the ocean bed.

blocks.question: Which mineral is formed by the decomposition of surface rocks?
blocks.explanation: Soluble constituents are removed, leaving a residual mass rich in bauxite.
option_feedback: Copper occurs in veins and lodes.
Gold is found in placer deposits.

blocks.title: Ferrous, non-ferrous and non-metallic minerals
blocks.body:
**Ferrous minerals** account for about **three-fourths** of the total value of the production of metallic minerals, and provide a strong base for metallurgical industries.

**Iron ore:** the basic mineral and the backbone of industrial development. India is rich in good-quality iron ores.
- **Magnetite** is the **finest** iron ore, with a very high content of iron, **up to 70 per cent**; it has excellent magnetic qualities, especially valuable in the electrical industry.
- **Hematite** is the most important industrial iron ore in terms of quantity used, with slightly lower iron content, **50 to 60 per cent**.
- The major iron ore belts are listed in the table: Odisha-Jharkhand, Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur, Ballari-Chitradurga-Chikkamagaluru-Tumakuru and Maharashtra-Goa.

**Manganese:** mainly used in the manufacture of **steel and ferro-manganese alloy**; nearly **10 kg of manganese** is required to make **one tonne of steel**. It is also used in bleaching powder, insecticides and paints.

**Non-ferrous minerals:** India's reserves and production are not very satisfactory. These minerals, which include **copper, bauxite, lead, zinc and gold**, play a vital role in metallurgical, engineering and electrical industries.
- **Copper:** India is **critically deficient** in copper. Being malleable, ductile and a good conductor, it is used in electrical cables, electronics and chemical industries. The **Balaghat** mines (Madhya Pradesh), the **Khetri** mines (Rajasthan) and **Singhbhum** (Jharkhand) are leading producers.
- **Bauxite:** though several ores contain aluminium, it is from **bauxite**, a clay-like substance, that **alumina and later aluminium** are obtained. Bauxite deposits form by the decomposition of a wide variety of rocks rich in aluminium silicates. **Aluminium** combines the **strength** of metals such as iron with **extreme lightness**, and also has **good conductivity and great malleability**. India's bauxite deposits are mainly found in the **Amarkantak plateau, Maikal hills and the plateau region of Bilaspur-Katni**. **Odisha** was the **largest bauxite-producing state** in India (2016-17); the **Panchpatmali** deposits in **Koraput** district are the most important bauxite deposits in the state.

**Non-metallic minerals:**
- **Mica:** made up of a series of **plates or leaves**; it splits easily into thin sheets, which can be clear, black, green, red, yellow or brown. Due to its excellent **di-electric strength**, low power loss factor, **insulating properties** and resistance to high voltage, mica is one of the most indispensable minerals in **electric and electronic industries**. Mica deposits are found on the northern edge of the **Chota Nagpur plateau**; the **Koderma-Gaya-Hazaribagh** belt of Jharkhand is the leading producer. In Rajasthan, the major mica area is around **Ajmer**; the **Nellore** mica belt of Andhra Pradesh is also important.

**Rock minerals:**
- **Limestone:** found in association with rocks composed of **calcium carbonates or calcium and magnesium carbonates**, in sedimentary rocks of most geological formations. It is the **basic raw material for the cement industry** and essential for **smelting iron ore** in the blast furnace.

blocks.title: Iron ore belts of India
blocks.body:
| Iron ore belt | Key mines / facts |
|---|---|
| **Odisha-Jharkhand** | high-grade hematite at **Badampahar** (Mayurbhanj and Kendujhar, Odisha); Gua and Noamundi (Singhbhum, Jharkhand) |
| **Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur** (Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra) | very high-grade hematite in the **Bailadila** hills of Bastar; 14 deposits; exported to Japan and South Korea via Visakhapatnam |
| **Ballari-Chitradurga-Chikkamagaluru-Tumakuru** (Karnataka) | large reserves; **Kudremukh** in the Western Ghats is a 100% export unit; ore sent as slurry by pipeline to a port near Mangaluru |
| **Maharashtra-Goa** | Goa and Ratnagiri; ore not of very high quality but efficiently exploited; exported through **Marmagao** |

blocks.explanation: Magnetite also has excellent magnetic qualities.
option_feedback: Bauxite is the ore of aluminium.
The chapter names magnetite as the finest.

blocks.question: Kudremukh iron ore mines are known for being:
options: a 100% export unit in the Western Ghats of Karnataka
blocks.explanation: The ore is sent as slurry through a pipeline to a port near Mangaluru.
option_feedback: Copper comes from Balaghat and Khetri.

blocks.title: The cost of mining and how to save minerals
blocks.body:
**Hazards of mining:**
- The **dust and noxious fumes** inhaled by miners make them vulnerable to **pulmonary (lung) diseases**.
- The risk of **collapsing mine roofs, inundation and fires** in coal mines is a constant threat to miners.
- **Water sources** in the region get **contaminated** due to mining.
- **Dumping of waste and slurry** leads to **degradation of land and soil**, and an increase in **stream and river pollution**.
Stricter safety regulations and implementation of environmental laws are essential to prevent mining from becoming a 'killer industry'.

**Conservation of minerals:** all of us appreciate our strong dependence on minerals. Industry and agriculture depend upon mineral deposits and the substances made from them. But:
- the total volume of workable mineral deposits is an **insignificant fraction (one per cent)** of the Earth's crust;
- mineral resources are being consumed rapidly, while the geological processes of mineral formation are so **slow** that the rate of replenishment is **infinitely small** compared with present rates of consumption;
- minerals are **finite and non-renewable**; continued extraction leads to **increasing costs** as mineral extraction comes from greater depths along with a **decrease in quality**.

**How to conserve:** use mineral resources in a **planned and sustainable** manner; use **improved technologies** that allow low-grade ores to be used at low costs; **recycle metals**, use **scrap metals** and other **substitutes**.

blocks.question: Which is a way to conserve minerals?
options: Recycling metals and using scrap and substitutes
blocks.explanation: Planned use, better technology for low-grade ores, recycling and substitutes conserve minerals.
option_feedback: That raises costs and lowers quality.
Improved technology should let us use low-grade ores too.

blocks.title: Coal, petroleum, natural gas and electricity
blocks.body:
Energy is needed to cook, to provide light and heat, to propel vehicles and to drive machinery in industries. It can be generated from fuel minerals like coal, petroleum, natural gas and uranium, and from electricity. Energy resources are classified as **conventional** (firewood, cattle dung cake, coal, petroleum, natural gas and electricity, both hydel and thermal) and **non-conventional** (solar, wind, tidal, geothermal, biogas and atomic energy). **Firewood and cattle dung cake** are most common in rural India; it is estimated that **more than 70 per cent** of the energy requirement in rural households is met by these two, but their use is becoming difficult due to decreasing forest area, and dung cake is better used as manure.

**Coal:** the **most abundantly available fossil fuel** in India. It provides a substantial part of the nation's energy needs: for **power generation**, energy to **industry** and **domestic** needs. India is highly dependent on coal for meeting its **commercial energy** requirements. Coal is formed by the **compression of plant material** over millions of years, and is found in a variety of forms depending on the degree of compression and the depth and time of burial (see the table).
- In India coal occurs in rock series of two main geological ages: **Gondwana**, a little over **200 million years** old, and **tertiary** deposits about **55 million years** old.
- The major resources of **Gondwana coal** (metallurgical coal) are in the **Damodar valley** (West Bengal-Jharkhand); **Jharia, Raniganj and Bokaro** are important coalfields. The **Godavari, Mahanadi, Son and Wardha** valleys also contain coal deposits.
- **Tertiary coals** occur in the north-eastern states of **Meghalaya, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland**.
- Coal is a **bulky material**, which loses weight on use as it is reduced to ash. So heavy industries and thermal power stations are located **on or near the coalfields**.

**Petroleum (mineral oil):** the next major energy source after coal. It provides fuel for heat and lighting, lubricants for machinery and raw materials for many manufacturing industries. **Petroleum refineries** act as a **'nodal industry'** for synthetic textile, fertiliser and numerous chemical industries.
- Most petroleum occurrences in India are associated with **anticlines and fault traps** in rock formations of the **tertiary age**. In regions of folding, anticlines or domes, oil is trapped in the crest of the upfold. The oil-bearing layer is a **porous limestone or sandstone** through which oil may flow; it is prevented from rising or sinking by intervening **non-porous layers**. Petroleum is also found in **fault traps** between porous and non-porous rocks. **Gas**, being lighter, usually occurs **above the oil**.
- **Mumbai High, Gujarat and Assam** are the major petroleum-producing areas. **Ankleshwar** is the most important field of Gujarat. **Assam** is the **oldest** oil-producing state; **Digboi, Naharkatia and Moran-Hugrijan** are its important oil fields.

**Natural gas:** an important **clean energy** resource, found in association with or without petroleum. It is used as a source of energy and as an industrial raw material in the **petrochemical** industry. It is considered an **environment-friendly fuel** because of **low carbon dioxide emissions**. Large reserves have been discovered in the **Krishna-Godavari basin**; along the west coast, the reserves of **Mumbai High** and allied fields are supplemented by finds in the **Gulf of Cambay**; the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** are also important. The **power and fertiliser** industries are the key users of natural gas; the use of **CNG (compressed natural gas)** for vehicles is gaining popularity.

**Electricity:** generated mainly in two ways: by **running water** which drives hydro turbines (**hydroelectricity**), and by **burning fuels** such as coal, petroleum and natural gas to drive turbines (**thermal power**).
- **Hydroelectricity** is generated by fast-flowing water, a **renewable** resource. India has a number of multipurpose projects like **Bhakra Nangal, Damodar Valley Corporation and the Kopili Hydel Project**.
- **Thermal electricity** is generated using coal, petroleum and natural gas; thermal power stations use **non-renewable** fossil fuels.

blocks.title: Types of coal
blocks.body:
| Type of coal | Features |
|---|---|
| **Peat** | decaying plants in swamps; low carbon, high moisture, low heating capacity |
| **Lignite** | low-grade brown coal, soft with high moisture; main reserves at **Neyveli** (Tamil Nadu), used for electricity |
| **Bituminous** | buried deep and subjected to higher temperatures; most popular commercial coal; metallurgical coal is high-grade bituminous for smelting iron |
| **Anthracite** | highest quality hard coal |

blocks.question: Why are thermal power stations located on or near coalfields?
options: Coal cannot be transported at all
Coal is bulky and loses weight on use as it turns to ash
blocks.explanation: Moving bulky coal is costly, so plants are built near the mines.
option_feedback: It can, but it is costly to move.

blocks.question: Which is the oldest oil-producing state of India?
blocks.explanation: Digboi, Naharkatia and Moran-Hugrijan are Assam's important fields.
option_feedback: Mumbai High is offshore Maharashtra but not the oldest.

blocks.title: Nuclear, solar, wind, biogas, tidal and geothermal
blocks.body:
The growing consumption of energy has made India increasingly dependent on fossil fuels. Rising prices of oil and gas and their potential shortages have raised uncertainties about the security of energy supply, with serious repercussions on economic growth. Increasing use of fossil fuels also causes serious environmental problems. So there is a pressing need to use **renewable energy** sources.

- **Nuclear or atomic energy:** obtained by **altering the structure of atoms**; when such an alteration is made, much energy is released as heat, which is used to generate electricity. **Uranium and thorium**, available in **Jharkhand** and the **Aravalli ranges of Rajasthan**, are used for generating atomic or nuclear power. The **monazite sands of Kerala** are also rich in **thorium**.
- **Solar energy:** India is a tropical country with enormous possibilities of tapping solar energy. **Photovoltaic technology** converts sunlight directly into electricity. One of the largest solar plants is near **Bhuj** (at Madhapur), where solar energy is used to **sterilise milk cans**. Solar energy can reduce the dependence of rural households on firewood and dung cakes, leaving more manure for agriculture.
- **Wind power:** India now ranks as a 'wind super power' in the world. The largest wind farm cluster is located in **Tamil Nadu from Nagarcoil to Madurai**; Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Gujarat, Kerala, Maharashtra and Lakshadweep also have important wind farms. **Nagarcoil and Jaisalmer** are well known for the effective use of wind energy.
- **Biogas:** shrubs, farm waste, animal and human waste are used to produce biogas for domestic consumption in rural areas. Decomposition of organic matter yields gas with **higher thermal efficiency** than kerosene, dung cake and charcoal. Plants using cattle dung are known as **'Gobar gas plants'**. They provide **twin benefits** to the farmer: **energy** and **improved quality of manure**. Biogas is the most efficient use of cattle dung; it improves the quality of manure and prevents the loss of trees and manure due to burning of fuel wood and cow dung cakes.
- **Tidal energy:** oceanic tides can be used to generate electricity. **Floodgate dams** are built across inlets. During high tide, water flows into the inlet and gets trapped when the gate is closed. After the tide falls outside the floodgate, the water retained flows back to the sea via a pipe that carries it through a **power-generating turbine**. In India, the **Gulf of Khambhat, the Gulf of Kachchh** in Gujarat on the western coast, and the **Gangetic delta in the Sunderban** region of West Bengal provide ideal conditions.
- **Geothermal energy:** heat and electricity produced by using the **heat from the interior of the Earth**. Temperature increases with depth; where the geothermal gradient is high, high temperatures are found at shallow depths, and groundwater absorbs heat from the rocks and rises to the surface as **hot springs**. Two experimental projects have been set up: one in the **Parvati valley near Manikarn** in **Himachal Pradesh** and the other in the **Puga Valley, Ladakh**.

**Conservation of energy:** energy is a basic requirement for economic development. We need a cautious approach to the judicious use of limited energy resources. As concerned citizens we can: use **public transport** instead of individual vehicles; **switch off** electricity when not in use; use **power-saving devices**; and use **non-conventional sources** of energy. After all, **'energy saved is energy produced'**.

blocks.title: Memory tricks
blocks.body:
- **Five modes of occurrence: "Very Bright Diamonds Please Others"** = Veins/lodes (igneous), Beds (sedimentary), Decomposition (bauxite), Placer (alluvial), Ocean (salt, magnesium, bromine).
- **Iron ore: "MAGnetite = MAGnificent, 70%"; hematite 50-60%.**
- **Coal ladder (worst to best): Peat → Lignite → Bituminous → Anthracite ("Please Let Better Arrive").**
- **Oil in Assam: "Digboi Never Misses"** = Digboi, Naharkatia, Moran-Hugrijan.
- **Geothermal = Parvati + Puga; Tidal = Khambhat, Kachchh, Sunderban.**
- **Nuclear plants on the map: "No Kid Taps Kettles"** = Narora, Kakrapara, Tarapur, Kalpakkam.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.body:
1. Saying hematite is the finest ore: **magnetite** is finest (up to 70%); hematite is the most used.
2. Calling bauxite a placer deposit: it forms by **decomposition of surface rocks**.
3. Saying lignite is the best coal: **anthracite** is the highest quality; lignite is low-grade brown coal.
4. Saying gas lies below oil: gas, being lighter, usually occurs **above** the oil.
5. Mixing up Gondwana coal (about 200 million years, Damodar valley) and tertiary coal (about 55 million years, north-east).
6. Calling thermal power renewable: it uses **non-renewable** fossil fuels; hydel power is renewable.

blocks.title: Try this in class
blocks.body: Make a 'mineral treasure hunt': students list ten objects at home and find the mineral in each (iron, aluminium, copper, mica, limestone). Then give outline maps and ask them to mark the five iron mines, four coal mines, six oil fields and seven power plants from the map list.

blocks.title: Think and explain
blocks.body: 'Energy saved is energy produced.' List three ways your family can save energy this week, and say which energy source each one saves.

blocks.title: Mastery challenge
blocks.body:
'Coal is the most important and abundant fossil fuel in India.' Justify with its uses and types (2025-26 sample paper idea), in about 120 words.

**Model answer:** Coal is the most abundantly available fossil fuel in India and provides a substantial part of the nation's energy needs. It is used for power generation, to supply energy to industry and for domestic needs; India is highly dependent on coal for its commercial energy, for example in metallurgy. Coal is found in different forms depending on compression, depth and time of burial: peat has low carbon and high moisture with low heating capacity; lignite is a low-grade brown coal mined at Neyveli and used for electricity; bituminous coal is the most popular commercial coal, and its high-grade metallurgical form is used to smelt iron in blast furnaces; anthracite is the highest-quality hard coal. Major fields like Jharia, Raniganj and Bokaro support heavy industries and thermal power plants.

blocks.title: Chapter summary
blocks.body:
- A mineral is a homogenous, naturally occurring substance with a definable internal structure; minerals occur in veins and lodes, beds, residual deposits, placer deposits and ocean waters.
- Ferrous minerals: iron ore (magnetite, hematite; four belts) and manganese. Non-ferrous: copper (Balaghat, Khetri), bauxite (Amarkantak, Maikal, Koraput). Non-metallic: mica (Koderma-Gaya-Hazaribagh). Rock minerals: limestone.
- Mining harms miners' health and the environment; minerals must be conserved through planned use, technology, recycling and substitutes.
- Conventional energy: coal (Gondwana, tertiary), petroleum (Mumbai High, Gujarat, Assam), natural gas (Krishna-Godavari, Mumbai High) and electricity (hydel, thermal).
- Non-conventional energy: nuclear, solar, wind, biogas, tidal and geothermal; energy saved is energy produced.

blocks.title: Board exam tips
blocks.body:
- The 2025-26 sample paper asked why setting up a bauxite industry in Odisha is advisable (Panchpatmali in Koraput; aluminium's strength, lightness, conductivity and malleability) and, as an alternative, why coal is the most important fossil fuel (uses and types).
- 3/5-mark favourites: modes of occurrence, iron ore belts, hazards of mining, conservation, coal, petroleum traps, non-conventional energy.
- **Map work:** iron ore mines, coal mines, oil fields, thermal and nuclear power plants (see the map list table).

blocks.back: A homogenous, naturally occurring substance with a definable internal structure.

blocks.front: Why does gas usually occur above oil?
blocks.back: Gas is lighter than oil, so it collects above it in anticlines and fault traps.

blocks.front: Name the four types of coal from lowest to highest quality.
